title: Google Chrome: use after free in XML, exploited (CVE-2026-125350)
summary: Google updated Chrome's stable channel on 9 November 2026 to 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux, and Chrome's Extended Stable channel the same day to 156.0.8078.96 for Windows and Mac. Both updates fix CVE-2026-125350, a use after free in XML, which the CVE record (published 10 November) says allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page, in Chrome before 157.0.8103.50. Google's post says: "Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild." CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 10 Nov 2026, due 24 Nov. Other browsers built on Chromium ship the fix on their own schedule: Brave in 1.99.56 (Chromium 157.0.8103.50, 10 November) and Vivaldi in 8.3.4191.35 ("8.3 minor update 2", 10 November, which Vivaldi says includes a fix for CVE-2026-125350). As read on 13 November 2026, Microsoft's Edge security notes name the fix only for Edge for Android (157.0.4341.53) and no fixed Edge for Mac. Wardlatch reads the version of each browser that is installed (the app's Info.plist on a Mac, dpkg's record of Chrome on Debian and Ubuntu); it never starts a browser.

files.label: Mac app
files.reviewWhenFixed: this Chrome, as installed, has the fix; if Chrome was open when it updated, it runs the old version until it restarts (Chrome's menu shows Relaunch), and Wardlatch can't see which version is running

reviewAbove.reason: this Chrome is on a newer line than the fixed ones (Extended Stable 156.0.8078.96, Stable 157.0.8103.50), and Google's notes for its builds don't list the fix for CVE-2026-125350: Chrome's Early Stable 158.0.8127.18/.19 shipped on 4 Nov, before the exploit was reported on 6 Nov, so whether this build has the fix is not known

versionFiles.fix: Update Chrome to 157.0.8103.50 or later (on a Mac 157.0.8103.50 or .51), or, on Chrome's Extended Stable channel, to 156.0.8078.96 or later: open Chrome, go to Settings, About Chrome, let it update, then press Relaunch. On Debian or Ubuntu: sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade google-chrome-stable, then restart Chrome.
versionFiles.lookedIn: the Info.plist of Chrome, Brave, Vivaldi and Microsoft Edge in /Applications and ~/Applications, and dpkg's record of google-chrome-stable

reviewFix: Restart Chrome (Chrome's menu shows Relaunch when an update is waiting), so the version that runs is the one installed.
safeText: no Google Chrome, Brave, Vivaldi or Microsoft Edge found in the places this check reads
notCovered: Opera and Arc, for which no fixed version was found as of 13 Nov 2026; Brave, Vivaldi and Edge anywhere but /Applications and ~/Applications, and on Linux; Chromium itself; Chrome's beta, dev and canary channels; Chrome installed by snap, Flatpak or an RPM; ChromeOS, Android and iOS; Electron apps; Windows. Brave's and Vivaldi's Info.plist were read from their published version formats, not from a real bundle on the Mac this was written on. Check each one's own release notes.
